system.summary: Cecil's 'new ciphre' of Sept 1559: a sign for a person (② = Earl of Arran) and signs for a sum (+ H oo = 200 crowns); only two groups used. Randolph's key R4851 (31 Aug 1559) in the same volume does not contain them.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched R4847, R4860 and the key record R4851 with the shared DECODE cookie.
R4847 is in clear except '② borrowed of me at his being at London + H oo'; R4860 has no cipher at all.
Checked R4851 (ff. 166-167, endorsed 'Rand. Ciphre. Aug. 31 1559'): Randolph's nomenclator, no ② sign, does not apply.
From context (Arran's secret passage through London to Cecil, late Aug 1559), ② = the Earl of Arran and '+ H oo' a sum of money.
Found both letters in Clifford's Sadler State Papers I (1809): 'Therle of Arrayn borrowed of me at his being at London 200 crowns', the cipher printed as deciphered by a contemporary hand.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): R4847: transcription.txt and the deciphered phrase copied verbatim from NOTES.md to texts/R4847_decryption.md, with Clifford 1809 linked; R4860 has no cipher (no transcription possible), Clifford linked.

Full-texts audit, R4860: checked the folder, the DECODE public API record and the record page for a transcription; there is none and none is possible, because the letter has no cipher (NOTES.md, images viewed 21 Sep 2026). Recorded as transcription_missing with that reason. The images could not be looked at again: DECODE serves them only to a signed-in session.

outcome.method_basis: The one ciphered phrase in R4847 is printed already deciphered in Clifford's Sadler State Papers I (1809), no. XXXVI ('Therle of Arrayn ... 200 crowns'), found by web search during the attempt; R4860 has no cipher.
outcome.notes: Printed in 1809. The cipher is two groups in one letter; the other letter is in clear. Catalogue entry 85 removed, no write-up.

texts.label: Cecil near Stamford to Sadler and Croft, 11 Sep 1559
texts.summary: William Cecil writes in clear to Sir Ralph Sadler and Sir James Croft at Berwick, with one phrase in the new cipher he had just sent them: 'Therle of Arrayn borrowed of me at his being at London 200 crowns', the Earl of Arran having passed secretly through London to Cecil in late August 1559. The letter is printed in full in Clifford, Sadler State Papers I (1809) no. XXXVI, with the phrase already deciphered.

reading_review.note: Rests on Clifford, Sadler State Papers I (1809) no. XXXVI p. 437, where the two ciphered groups are printed deciphered: 'Therle of Arrayn borrowed of me at his being at London 200 crowns' (texts/R4847_decryption.md). The cipher is only those two groups inside a clear letter; with them the sentence reads in full. The repository text is the one phrase, an external pointer for the rest of the letter.

A copy of the clear text would not be a transcription of a cipher. Nothing unblocks this; the record's own 'graphic signs, numerical' label is what needs correcting.
texts.summary: Cecil writes from London 'at midnight' to Sadler and Croft; the letter is entirely in clear and printed in Clifford, Sadler State Papers I (1809) no. XCVII, pp. 526-527.
texts.note: No cipher on either page, so there is no transcription to give; the letter is listed here only because DECODE grouped it with R4847. Nothing to read as cipher (24 Oct 2026, reading gate).
